facts.statement: Fossils were found in the uppermost portion of the Maastrichtian-age Serra da Galga Formation of the Bauru Group in Uberaba, Minas Gerais.
facts.quote: These fossils were found in the uppermost portion of the Maastrichtian-age Serra da Galga Formation of the Bauru Group, in Uberaba, Minas Gerais.

facts.statement: The species name honors Luiz Carlos Borges Ribeiro, the director of the Centro de Pesquisas Paleontológicas Lewellyn Price, for his support.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to Uberaba and the species name honors Luiz Carlos Borges Ribeiro, the director of the Centro de Pesquisas Paleontológicas Lewellyn Price, for his support.

facts.statement: Uberabatitan lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense de lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests the species lived in conditions of extreme aridity and heat.
facts.quote: La cantidad, diversidad y grado de preservación de los fósiles permitió a los científicos entender la evolución de la familia de los titanosaurios y establecer que la especie vivió en condiciones extremas de aridez y calor.

facts.statement: Like other sauropods, Uberabatitan underwent rapid, uninterrupted growth early in life.
facts.quote: Uberabatitan, like other sauropods, underwent rapid, uninterrupted growth early in life.

facts.statement: Uberabatitan is the most recent titanosaur from the Bauru Group of the same clade and location, while Baurutitan and Trigonosaurus belong to deeper and therefore older layers.
facts.quote: Es el más reciente de los titanosaurios del Grupo Bauru del mismo clado y lugar, Baurutitan y Trigonosaurus, pero estos últimos pertenecen a capas más profundas y por lo tanto más antiguas.

facts.statement: The time range for Uberabatitan is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
